title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 19 (Determination of rules of procedure)

content.overview: Section 19 allows the parties to agree on the procedure to be followed by the arbitral tribunal. Failing agreement, the tribunal may conduct the proceedings in the manner it considers appropriate, subject to Part I. The tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 or the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
content.glance: Party agreement on procedure first; otherwise tribunal decides; CPC and Evidence Act do not bind the tribunal.
content.study: Party agreement controls procedure. Failing agreement, the tribunal conducts proceedings as it considers appropriate, subject to Part I. The tribunal is not bound by the CPC or the Indian Evidence Act.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 19 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State any party agreement on procedure. II. Apply residual tribunal power. III. Note CPC/Evidence Act non-binding. IV. Apply s. 18 fairness. V. Conclude.
